title: Mohd. Asif vs Rahis Ahmed 1 on 8 May, 2017
full_text: Mohd. Asif vs Rahis Ahmed 1 on 8 May, 2017 IN THE COURT OF MS. AMRITA TONK, METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE (NI ACT)-1, CENTRAL: ROOM NO.337, TIS HAZARI COURT COMPLEX, DELHI Mohd. Asif Khan VERSUS Rahis Ahmed JUDGMENT Part A - The lis at a glance A. Serial No. of the Case: 531878/16 B. Date of Institution: 02.06.2010 C. Name of the Complainant: Mohd. Asif, S/o Sh. Mohd. Fazel, 106 (SF), Gali Kandely Kashan, Fatehpuri, Chandni Chowk, Delhi- 110006. D. Name of Accused: Rahis Ahmed @ Rais Khan, S/o Sh. Ahmed Agha Khan, Prop of M/s Sameer Offset Printers, at Katra Shekh Chand Bazar, Lal Kuan, Delhi- 110006. Also residing at: 1138, Baradari, Tilak Bazar, Delhi- 110006. E. Offence complained of: Dishonor of cheque - culpable u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. F. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty. G. Final Order: Acquitted H. Judgment reserved on: 18.04.2017 I. Judgment pronounced on: 08.05.2017 Part B - A brief statement of reasons for the decision (As mandated u/s 355(i) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.) Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 1 CC No. 531878/16 1. This judgment shall decide upon the complaint filed by Mohd. Asif, (hereinafter referred to as the 'Complainant') under Section 138 , Negotiable Instruments Act, (hereinafter referred to as the 'the NI Act ') against Rahis Ahmed (hereinafter referred to as the 'Accused'). 2. The case of the Complainant, in brief, is that the Accused had entered into an agreement dated 06.03.2008 with the Complainant's brother as per which the Complainant's brother had agreed to advance interest free loan of Rs. 1,00,000/- to the Accused and the Accused had agreed to employ the Complainant's brother for printing job. The Accused failed to provide employment to the Complainant's brother and thus, the Complainant demanded the repayment of the loan amount. In discharge of his liability, the Accused issued cheque bearing number 000009 dated 10.03.2010 for the amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- drawn on Bank of India, Hamdard Dawakhana Branch, Gali Qasimjan, Bazar Lal Kuan, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as the 'cheque in question') in favor of the Complainant. The Complainant presented the said cheque in his bank but the cheque in question was dishonoured with the remarks "insufficient funds" vide bank returning memo dated 21.04.2010. Thereafter the Complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 10.05.2010 to the Accused, but Accused failed to make the payment of dishonoured cheque within the statutory period of fifteen days. Hence, the Complainant filed the present complaint. 3. In his pre-summoning evidence, the complainant has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. CW1/1. He reiterated the contents of complaint and placed on record the original agreement dated 06.03.2008 as Ex. CW1/A, original cheque bearing number 000009 dated 10.03.2010 for the amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- (in figures) drawn on Bank of India, Hamdard Dawakhana Branch, Gali Qasimjan, Bazar Lal Kuan, New Delhi as Ex.CW1/B, cheque returning memo dated 21.04.2010 as Ex.CW1/C (Colly), legal demand notice dated 10.05.2010 as Ex. CW1/D, postal receipt as Ex. CW1/E and UPC as Ex. CW1/F. Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 2 CC No. 531878/16 4. Accused was summoned by the Court for the offence punishable u/s 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act. Notice of accusation u/s 251 Cr.P.C. was served upon the Accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. Thereafter, the Accused cross-examined the Complainant/CW1. The Complainant also examined his brother Mohd. Suhail as CW2. CW2 was then cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the Accused and discharged. The Complainant submitted that he did not wish to lead further evidence, and thus CE was closed. 6. All the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against the Accused was put to him and his statement was recorded in terms of Sec 313 Cr.P.C . The Accused admitted his signatures on the cheque in question as well as factum of issuance of the cheque in question to the Complainant as well as the factum of dishonor of the cheque in question. He denied receipt of the legal demand notice, however, he admitted that the address appearing on the same is correct. He admitted his signatures on Ex. CW1/A, however, he pleaded ignorance of the contents of the same. He stated that the cheque in question had been given to the Complainant for purchase of material for the purpose of business jointly run by him and the Complainant. 7. Thereafter, the Accused moved the application u/s 315 Cr.P.C. and the same was allowed. Pursuant to the same, the Accused stepped in the witness box as DW1. He was examined in chief, cross-examined and discharged. Thereafter, the Accused submitted that he did not wish to lead further evidence and thus DE was closed and the matter was listed for final arguments. At this stage it is pertinent to mention that the evidence in the present matter has not been recorded in a summary manner, but it has been recorded in full with examination and cross- examination of the witnesses. In light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mehsana Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd. vs. Shreeji Cab Co.& Ors. [2014 CriLJ Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 3 CC No. 531878/16 1953], this Court is inclined to rely on the evidence, which has been recorded by the learned Transferor Court. 8. Final arguments were addressed by the respective Counsels of both the parties. Ld. Counsel for the Complainant submitted that the Accused has admitted his signature on the cheque in question as well as issuance of the cheque to the Complainant and thus the presumptions u/s 118 and 139 NI Act have arisen in favor of the Complainant. Ld. Counsel for the Complainant has argued that the Accused has failed to rebut the presumptions arisen in favor of the Complainant. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel has argued that the Complainant has not been able to prove that the cheque in question was issued against debt/liability amount as the liability amount as per the allegations of the Complainant was Rs. 1,00,000/- whereas the cheque amount is stated to be Rs. 1,20,000/-. It is further argued the Accused had handed over the cheque in question in blank for the purpose of purchase of goods for the printing press and that the amount in the cheque has been wrongly filled in by the Complainant. It is argued that the same is evident from the fact that the amount written in words and figures differs. Ld. Counsel has also argued that the Accused had not received the legal demand notice and the Complainant had intentionally sent the legal demand notice at the earlier address of the Accused despite knowing that the Accused had shifted from the premises. Ld. Counsel has argued that the Accused has successfully rebutted the statutory presumptions. 9. I have heard the submissions and have carefully perused the record. For properly appreciating the facts of the case and submissions of both the parties, a reference is necessary to the relevant statutory provisions. The following are the essential ingredients for constituting the offence under Section 138 NI Act:  Person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for payment of certain amount of money to another person from out of that account; Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 4 CC No. 531878/16  The cheque should have been issued for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability;  That cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date of which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier;  That cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank;  The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid;  The drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice. It is only when all of the above-mentioned ingredients are satisfied that the person who had drawn the cheque can be deemed to have committed an offence under Section 138 of the Act. 10. Issuance of the Cheque in question - In the present case, the Accused has admitted his signatures on the cheque in question. However, he has denied filling in the particulars in the cheque in question. It is no longer res integra, that no law requires that whole body of the cheque should be filled by the drawer himself. If the signatures on the cheque are admitted, the same is sufficient in terms of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Ravi Chopra vs. State And Anr. [(2008) (2) LRC 118] In the present case, the Accused has Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 5 CC No. 531878/16 admitted having drawn the cheques on a bank account maintained in his name & having signed the same. Thus, the presumption under Section 118 and section 139 are raised. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rangappa vs. Sri Mohan , [AIR 2010 SC 1898] observed: "Once the cheque relates to the account of the accused and he accepts and admits the signatures on the said cheque, then initial presumption as contemplated under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act has to be raised by the Court in favour of the complainant." 11. Presentation of the Cheque for payment and the same being returned un- paid- The cheque in question had been presented for payment by the Complainant and the same was returned back unpaid. The same has not been denied by the Ac- cused. Ex. CW1/B was returned unpaid with the remarks "Insufficient funds" vide bank returning memo Ex. CW1/C. 12. Legal demand notice to be sent within 30 days of return of cheque and failure on the part of the Accused to make the payment within fifteen days of receipt of legal demand notice - As per the evidence on record, the communica- tion of dishonor of the cheque in question was given to the Accused by the Com- plainant vide legal demand notice dated 10.05.2010. The notice has been given within the stipulated period. The Accused in his statement recorded u/s 313 Cr.P.C. has denied receipt of the legal notice. To substantiate the factum of service of the legal demand notice, the Complainant has also filed the postal receipt and UPC. At this point, it is important to refer to the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in C.C. Alvi Haji V. Palapetty Muhammed & Anr. [2007 STPL(DC) 952 SC] wherein the Hon'ble Court held that even if the ac- cused didn't receive the legal demand notice he can pay the cheque amount within 15 days of service of summons from the court but if he fails, he can't contend that Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 6 CC No. 531878/16 he has not received the legal demand notice. The relevant extract is reproduced herein below:- " 17. It is also to be borne in mind that the requirement of giving of notice is a clear departure from the rule of Criminal Law, where there is no stipulation of giving of a notice before filing a complaint. Any drawer who claims that he did not receive the notice sent by post, can, within 15 days of receipt of summons from the court in respect of the complaint under Section 138 of the Act, make payment of the cheque amount and submit to the Court that he had made payment within 15 days of receipt of summons (by receiving a copy of complaint with the summons) and, therefore, the complaint is liable to be re- jected. A person who does not pay within 15 days of receipt of the summons from the Court along with the copy of the com- plaint under Section 138 of the Act, can- not obviously contend that there was no proper service of notice as required under Section 138 , by ignoring statutory pre- sumption to the contrary under Section 27 of the G.C. Act and Section 114 of the Evi- dence Act. In our view, any other interpre- tation of the proviso would defeat the very object of the legislation. As observed in Bhaskaran's case (supra), if the "giving of notice" in the context of Clause (b) of the proviso was the same as the "receipt" of notice" a trickster cheque drawer would get the premium to avoid receiving the no- tice by adopting different strategies and escape from legal consequences of Section 138 of the Act." In the present case the Accused appeared in Court on 16.11.2012 but till date he has not shown any intention to make the payment of cheque amount to the com- plainant. Thus in view of the above said precedent, the Accused cannot take the plea that the legal demand notice was not duly served on him. Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 7 CC No. 531878/16 13. Legally enforceable debt or liability- It is the case of the complainant that the Accused had taken an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- from the brother of the Complainant as interest free loan. The Complainant during his cross examination had stated that he had given money to his brother and the same has been further advanced by his brother to the Accused. He stated that he has in his possession a document evidencing the fact that he had given an amount of Rs. 1,35,000/- to his brother, however, he admitted that he had not filed on record any such document. It is pertinent to note that the cheque in question is alleged to have been issued for an amount of Rs. 1,20,000/-. The amount mentioned in the cheque in question in words varies from the amount mentioned in figures. Section 18 of the NI Act provides that in case the amount undertaken or ordered to be paid is stated differently in figures and in words, the amount stated in words shall be the amount undertaken or ordered to be paid. The amount in words is stated as "only one lakh twenty two thousands". The agreement Ex. CW1/A relied upon by the Complainant states that the brother of the Complainant shall be at liberty to take back the amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- after giving three months' notice to the Accused. The agreement also refers to a monthly remuneration of Rs. 5,000/- agreed to be paid by Accused to the brother of the Complainant. The Complainant has conceded that a loan of Rs. 1,00,000/- had been advanced to the Accused, whereas the cheque in question is stated to have been issued for a higher amount. On being cross-examined with respect to this, the Complainant had stated that the difference in amount was on account of a settlement for the purpose of dues/monthly profits. Admittedly, no such settlement has been mentioned in the complaint has well as the affidavit of the Complainant. No evidence has been brought forth by the Complainant to establish that an amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- was due to him by the Accused. CW2, who is the brother of the Complainant has in his testimony deposed that the cheque in question had been issued to him towards his salary. Thus, there are inconsistences in the case of the Complainant which have been brought out by Ld. Counsel for the Accused during cross examination of the Complainant witnesses. The complainant has failed to prove Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 8 CC No. 531878/16 on record that the Accused owed liability to the extent of amount mentioned in the cheque in question, as on the date of filing the complaint or that the cheque was issued in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability of the Accused. It has been held by Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Supply House vs. Ullas , [2006 Cri.L.J. 4330], that in order to deem that one had committed offence under Section 138 , the amount covered by the cheque shall be either in discharge of the liability incurred by the drawer, either in full or in part. It cannot in any way in excess of the liability incurred. The Hon'ble High Court of Bombay in M/s Pawan Enterprises vs. Satish H. Verma [2003 Crl. L. J. 2146] held that if the liability is less than the cheque amount, no offence under Section 138 NI Act would be made out. A similar view had been taken by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of M/s Elite Appliances Limited vs. M/s Sahni Builders Private Limited [Crl. Misc. (M) No. 3632/2001], wherein the Hon'ble High Court had referred to the case of M/s Pawan Enterprises vs. Satish H. Verma [supra]. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that the amount of the cheque should be same as that of the liability either in whole or in part. 14. In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the view that the Complainant has failed to discharge the burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the Accused whereas the Accused has succeeded in rebutting the presumption of legal liability. Accordingly, the Accused is acquitted of the charges leveled against him. Previous bail bonds stand discharged. Fresh bail bonds in terms of Section 437 A Cr.P.C. be filed. File be consigned to Record Room after due compliance. * Announced in the open court. (Amrita Tonk) MM - (NI Act )-Central-01/THC/Delhi 08.05.2017 Mohd. Asif VERSUS Rahis Ahmed 9 CC No. 531878/16
